links: Dense 1.6 bar air increases lift per wing area
Sun-warmed volcanic rock generates daily thermal updrafts
Sparse highland carrion requires wide foraging ranges

skill.effect: The creature rides rising air currents to climb steadily without tiring. You can watch it soar effortlessly upward on invisible thermal columns.

chains.weakness: Ground-bound in thick fog or windless dawn when thermals fail
observe: Wind ripples shimmering over dark basalt ridges
It banking silently in a rising spiral
Feather edges flaring to catch the updraft

journal.en: It reads the mountain’s breath before it reads the sky.

plausibility.summary: Either cut mass to ~12–22 kg for a 2.4 m wingspan high-aspect soarer, or keep ~85 kg but specify wingspan ~5.5–7 m+ and stress punctuated thermal hopping plus ridge soaring (not condor-effortless all-day float); optionally note partial quadruped/biped launch from cliffs (F2) to limit takeoff power

links: High-altitude UV radiation reaches 1.4× sea level values
Diurnal hunting demands high contrast vision
Eyes evolved large corneas and tapetum for ground detection

skill.effect: The creature scans the horizon with its specialized eyes to locate hidden remains. You can see it identify distant carcasses and mark bone deposits that were previously concealed.

chains.weakness: Blinded by sudden glare or dense morning fog
observe: Nictitating membrane sweeping across a glossy pupil
Head tilting to isolate shapes against bright sky
Salt crystals on distant bones flashing under sun

journal.en: Its eyes are tuned to the mountain’s harsh light.

plausibility.summary: Keep large eyes + UV-absorbing corneal/lenticular pigments or cone oil droplets (D23 parallel); replace tapetum with dual foveae or area centralis for ground/carion search; optionally weaker tapetum benefit only for dawn-fog foraging (F8/F16), with glare vulnerability retained
fixes: Keep large eyes + UV-absorbing corneal/lenticular pigments or cone oil droplets (D23 parallel); replace tapetum with dual foveae or area centralis for ground/carion search; optionally weaker tapetum benefit only for dawn-fog foraging (F8/F16), with glare vulnerability retained

analogues.organism: Turkey vulture (Cathartes aura) and African white-backed vulture (Gyps africanus) for distance carrion vision; reindeer (Rangifer tarandus) for UV-blocking lens/pigment at high exposure (terrestrial analog for UV screen, not tapetum)
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Dense atmosphere lowers terminal velocity and reduces fall impact
Bones fused, hollowed, and air-sac connected to lungs

skill.effect: The creature's hollow bones cushion its landings, allowing it to touch down without injury. You can watch it drift through the air with complete silence.

chains.weakness: Vulnerable to direct blunt strikes and heavy impact
observe: Feathering gaps that hum softly in wind
Soft landing on a narrow cliff lip
Pulsing air sac visible at the throat base

journal.en: A skeleton of air and stone, it trades hardness for the sky.

plausibility.summary: Hollow, air-sac-linked pneumatic skeleton is the standard mass-reduction package for volant vertebrates; it trades impact resistance for lower wing loading. Slightly higher gravity (F2, D6) works against it but is modest (+5%); denser air (F4) and lower terminal velocity (D16/F4) reduce fall injury risk, aligning with the stated fall-damage mitigation. Elevated pO2 (D10/F5) supports the aerobic cost of flight muscles and digestion in a large flier.

analogues.organism: Birds universally (e.g. chicken/songbird pneumatic vertebrae and long bones); ostrich retains reduced pneumaticity; pterosaurs as extinct analog for extreme pneumatization
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Highland diet consists of tough hides and dry bones
Ingests volcanic grit from mineral seeps to macerate food

skill.effect: It grinds bones and tough flesh with its gritty gizzard, steadily restoring its own energy with each meal.

chains.weakness: Requires regular access to volcanic grit or suffers indigestion
observe: Pecking at basalt outcrops and licking salt seeps
Crushing a femur against a rock ledge
Mineral crust staining the base of its beak

journal.en: It carries the mountain in its belly.

plausibility.summary: Carrion-plus-bone diet (D27) selects for gastric mill function; ingested silicate grit is widespread on Earth for grinding tough plant matter and bone fragments. Volcanic highlands supply basalt grit and mineral seeps (F23, D23—same pressure as espinodo/gastrolith lore). Higher oxygen partial pressure (D10) supports faster aerobic gut metabolism; unchanged need to visit grit sources is realistic (gastrolith residency time is limited in birds).
fixes: Carrion-plus-bone diet (D27) selects for gastric mill function; ingested silicate grit is widespread on Earth for grinding tough plant matter and bone fragments. Volcanic highlands supply basalt grit and mineral seeps (F23, D23—same pressure as espinodo/gastrolith lore). Higher oxygen partial pressure (D10) supports faster aerobic gut metabolism; unchanged need to visit grit sources is realistic (gastrolith residency time is limited in birds).

analogues.organism: Lammergeier/bearded vulture (Gypaetus barbatus) bone consumption; galliform gizzard + grit (e.g. domestic fowl); crocodilian gastroliths for grinding

body_plan.origin: Derived from a bipedal predator lineage that shifted to aerial scavenging

temperament: Opportunistic, patient, territorial over updrafts, avoids live predators
secrets: Fossilized wing bones found in the sunken lava tube
Albino variant with translucent feathers spotted on the windward cliff edge
moments: On a windless evening, it stands on a basalt outcrop, wings taut against the cooling air, waiting for tomorrow’s thermals to rise while carrion drifts silently in the fog below.

journal.en: It reads the mountain’s breath before it reads the sky.
Where others see stone, it sees a ladder to the clouds.
